summary: WorldEntity's non-StableId identity/provenance strings remain unbounded at PR #293 exact head 91b6e273c0c21326dfbfe9c5ee5227e99f26933e: checkedNonEmpty only enforces string/non-empty/no-control-character semantics, then kind plus origin.worldId/regionId/generator/recipeKey are retained in registered records. The new 65,536-byte string budget only applies inside persistentState. A caller can therefore register records carrying arbitrarily large top-level provenance strings, creating unbounded per-record memory and duplicate-diagnostic amplification outside the bounded-state closure. Add an explicit per-field or aggregate metadata byte budget before storage, with limit-1/limit/limit+1 regression coverage for kind and at least one origin field; do not widen this into a StableId redesign.
evidence: PR #293 current head 91b6e273c0c21326dfbfe9c5ee5227e99f26933e is mergeable and explicitly bounds persistentState depth/nodes/string bytes, but src/shared/Reality/WorldEntity.luau checkedNonEmpty has no length or byte check.

At the same exact head, cloneOrigin passes origin.worldId, optional regionId, generator, and recipeKey through checkedNonEmpty and freezes them into the stored origin; ownRecord/new likewise accept kind through checkedNonEmpty.

WorldEntity.isId separately caps entity IDs at 256 bytes, so this finding is intentionally limited to the other retained metadata/provenance strings rather than claiming StableId/WorldEntity IDs are unbounded.

The concurrently published event evt-20260811-085405-k3m9v6-worldentity-boundary-gap covers missing exact depth/node acceptance and registered-lifecycle atomic-rejection regressions; it does not cover top-level metadata byte bounds.

Repository PR/issue searches for WorldEntity metadata/string-limit/oversized origin-kind-recipeKey wording found no existing lane or PR addressing this top-level metadata budget gap. No production code was changed and no tests were run because HG-CAPACITY-MINING is FINDING-ONLY.
